prereg.kind: ANALYSIS (successor program design), not an arm

mechanism: Turn-level forensic accounting of an LLM coding-agent's decision loop on ARC-AGI-3, using the full transcript corpus of a certified benchmark run. Unit definitions matter and had been conflated: environment actions (entries in taaf game_run.history), ACTING TURNS (history entries with generated_tokens>0 -- a batch's tokens land on its last action), ANALYZER INVOCATIONS (one system-prompted request), and LLM GENERATIONS ([MODEL RESPONSE META] records). On the certified field-floor artifact those are 1639 / 424 / 449 / 1181. Each generation was classified by whether its python tool call invokes action(...) (acting) or not (inspection-only), by traceback presence in the tool result, by finish_reason, by tool_call_count==0, and by code idiom (segmentation, .ascii, transitions, animation(), BFS/heapq/frontier/beam search). Each action was classified by immediate repetition, coordinate re-use for click actions (ACTION6), RESET, and by whether it falls on the terminal never-cleared level (index >= sum(actions_per_level[:levels_completed])). Dead time per game = final_wallclock_seconds minus the wallclock of the last action of the last cleared level.
summary: 54.0% of acting turns are spent on a level the run never clears; 62.1% of LLM generations execute no environment action and carry 49.7% of all generated characters; 53.5% of turns fire exactly one action while 12.2% fire >=8 and carry 46.9% of all actions; median 88% of each game's wallclock elapses AFTER its last level clear (15/25 games >=80%, 8 games 100%). Tool-call FORMAT failures and finish_reason=length are both 0.0% -- two standing hypotheses die. The productive segment clears a level every 6.96 turns; the marginal turn (measured from a 3x-budget replicate) is worth 21% of the average turn. Pricing waste-recovery on the measured elasticity (epsilon=0.17 above the operating point) gives an upper bound of +4.0 levels: eliminating ALL inspection, ALL tracebacks and ALL request timeouts is a x2.16 budget multiplier worth lc 28->32, LB ~1.78. Two instruments were found broken: hard_noop_guard is armed and has NEVER fired in 5255 actions because board_signature() hashes the FULL grid while the games render per-step ticking HUD strips; and a 20-pass x 25-game reference artifact already on disk (max-over-clones / mean-over-clones = 2.97) had never been read. A predecessor claim is corrected: the agent DOES query the harness's transitions view (16.3% of generations) -- what it does not do is SEARCH (5.8% search idioms, 0.2% explicit candidate scoring) despite the system prompt recommending BFS by name.
lesson: When an agent loop saturates against a resource, decompose the loop into its true units before pricing any fix -- and price every candidate fix on the MEASURED elasticity of the resource it consumes, not on the average productivity of that resource. Here one measurement does two opposite jobs: a low elasticity (0.17) proves that recovering wasted budget is nearly worthless (perfect recovery is bounded at +14% of the metric), and the SAME low elasticity proves that spending that resource is nearly free -- which inverts the design rule from 'eliminate waste' to 'convert the surplus resource into the scarce one'. Two transferable corollaries: (1) a guard that has never fired may be one that CANNOT -- check whether its key can ever repeat in the observed state stream, because a full-state hash is uninformative in any environment carrying a per-step counter, timer or HUD; (2) long-horizon agent runs degenerate measurably rather than merely plateauing -- at 3x horizon this agent tripled its no-tool-call response rate to 16.5% of generated tokens and 5x'd its exact-duplicate code re-runs, with 93% of the degeneration in the final third.
why_informative: This is the negative result that redirects the remaining campaign. The program was about to be aimed at 'the agent wastes turns' -- a hypothesis the data confirms in magnitude (54% dead turns, 62% action-free generations) and refutes in usefulness. Because recovered waste re-enters the system as budget, and budget elasticity above the operating point was independently measured at 0.17, the entire waste-recovery family is bounded at +4 levels / LB ~1.8 -- inside a ceiling already owned by free nightly redraws. That closes a family before a single GPU-hour is spent on it and forces the program onto the only remaining lever: raising the value of a turn at constant turn count (x1.60 for the 2.5 tier, i.e. converting 52% of dead turns into cleared levels). It also supplies the first quantitative target definition the campaign has had, and two instrument repairs that were invisible until the loop was decomposed.

measured.vehicle: certified field-floor artifact (lc_total 28, mean_score 6.173, 1639 actions); transcripts pulled read-only and verified dict-identical to the on-disk benchmark.json
measured.score_arithmetic_retry_allowance: going k->k+1 cleared levels at uniform action ratio r beats staying at k iff r < sqrt((k+2)/k): unbounded at k=0, 1.73 at k=1, 1.41 at k=2, 1.13 at k=7; 20 of 25 games sit at k<=1

sealed_reading_rule: NONE -- this row is an ANALYSIS, not an arm, and carries no verdict on any mechanism. The two successor arms it specifies (P1 persistent tool namespace, P2 reset-anchored episodic retry) carry their own sealed bands (SIGNAL lc>=37 / NULL 22-36 / HARM <=21 at n=2 seeds against a comparator mean of 29.0) and their own MANDATORY delivery instruments read BEFORE the effect (P1 notes-write-rate >=30%, P2 attempt()-call-rate >=25%); below those thresholds the arm is logged as a DELIVERY FAILURE, never as a mechanism null.
robustness: Every transcript statistic is computed on an artifact whose benchmark.json was checked for dict-equality against the certified on-disk copy, so the numbers attach to the sealed lc-28/6.173 record. The turn taxonomy is reproduced on a second independent 25-game artifact at 3x budget and on five older-generation configs; the qualitative ordering (action-free generations 35-62%, format failures ~0, search idioms <6%) holds across all seven. The elasticity used for pricing is the pre-registered sealed value from exp 39, not re-fit here. The 2.97 clone ratio comes from a weaker June-02 config and is labelled as evidence that per-clone variance is large in this environment, NOT as this config's ratio.
honest_caveats: (1) The 6.96 turns-per-level conversion rate is measured on levels the agent CAN solve; applying it to dead turns is optimistic, and at the marginal games' observed 15-20 turns/level the LB 2.50 target becomes unreachable at 17 turns/game. (2) The clone-aggregation-is-a-mean reading of make_benchmark_kaggle_official_110 is INFERRED from source (110 independent GameAPI entries, n_passes=1, equal weights), not host-confirmed. (3) The interior (HUD-excluded) no-op rate -- the number that prices the guard repair -- is still UNKNOWN; the frames exist in intermediate_states.pkl and the measurement costs about one CPU-hour. (4) Character counts are used as a token proxy throughout.
disposition: ADOPTED as the successor program. First push-ready arm: P1 (persistent tool namespace), 2 seeds, 4.4 GPU-h, 0 submission slots, gated on scripts/local_gate.py. A prerequisite CPU-only instrument week (P0) must verify RESET-to-level-start semantics on the real simulator before P2 is built. Honest ceiling stated to the principal: lc 33-38 / LB 1.9-2.1 by 2026-11-02; P(LB>=2.50) ~10-15%; top-10 is not reachable by per-turn value alone at 17 turns/game.
